findings.title: The homepage declares no organization or local-business entity
findings.evidence: The homepage (https://books.toscrape.com/) has no Organization, LocalBusiness or equivalent entity in its JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa, after traversing any @graph fully. There is no explicit machine-readable statement of which brand this site belongs to.

evidence_detail.method: JSON-LD @graph traversal, Microdata itemtype and RDFa typeof checked for an Organization, LocalBusiness or Corporation node on the homepage
evidence_detail.expected: an Organization or LocalBusiness node on the homepage

suggested_action.summary: Add one Organization (or LocalBusiness, if there is a physical location) node to the homepage, in JSON-LD, with a stable identifier.
how: Include at minimum name, url, and logo.
Give it an @id so other structured data on the site can reference it rather than duplicating it.
Add sameAs links to profiles the brand actually controls.
suggested_action.mechanism: This is the single node a system uses to resolve 'this site' into 'this real-world brand'. Without it, every other page's content is attributed to an inferred entity rather than a declared one.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the homepage and confirm an Organization node with a name and url parses successfully.

findings.title: No structured data of any kind was found on the sampled pages
findings.evidence: None of the 21 sampled content pages carry JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa. A machine can read the text but has no explicit signal for what kind of thing each page describes or which entity it belongs to.

evidence_detail.method: presence of any parseable JSON-LD, Microdata itemtype or RDFa typeof, checked across every sampled content page
evidence_detail.expected: at least some structured data, of any of the three formats

suggested_action.summary: Add structured data for at least the organisation identity and the page types this site actually has, in JSON-LD.
how: Start with an Organization node on the homepage.
Add the type each template warrants: Product for product pages, Article for editorial content, and so on.
JSON-LD in a single script block in the page head is the easiest to maintain and validate.
suggested_action.mechanism: Structured data lets a machine classify content and resolve which real-world entity a page is about, without inferring it from prose. Its absence does not block reading the page, but it leaves classification to inference, which is less reliable.
suggested_action.verification: Run the page through a structured-data validator and confirm at least one recognised type is detected.

findings.title: Content pages declare no canonical URL
findings.evidence: 21 of 21 sampled content pages carry no rel=canonical link. Without one, a crawler that reaches the same content through a different URL, for example with a tracking parameter or a trailing slash, has to guess which address is the real one. Examples: https://books.toscrape.com/, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: presence of a parsed rel=canonical link on sampled content pages
evidence_detail.expected: a self-referencing canonical on every content page

suggested_action.summary: Add a self-referencing rel=canonical to every content template, pointing at the absolute preferred URL of that page.
how: Emit the canonical from the route's own definition so it is always the page's preferred absolute URL.
Use the same scheme, host and trailing-slash form as the sitemap, so the two do not disagree.
suggested_action.mechanism: A canonical consolidates the signals for one piece of content onto one address. Without it, parameterised and duplicated variants compete with each other and none accumulates the full weight.
suggested_action.verification: Request each URL and confirm the canonical matches the URL that was requested.

findings.title: No robots.txt is published
findings.evidence: A request for https://books.toscrape.com/robots.txt returned 404. No robots.txt means no crawler restrictions, so this does not block anything. It does mean there is nowhere to declare a sitemap or to state a deliberate policy for training versus retrieval crawlers.

evidence_detail.method: single request for /robots.txt recorded in the snapshot

suggested_action.summary: Publish a robots.txt that declares the sitemap and states an explicit policy for training and retrieval crawlers.
how: Serve /robots.txt as text/plain.
Add a Sitemap: line pointing at the sitemap index.
Decide deliberately whether to allow training crawlers; leaving it undeclared is a decision made by default rather than on purpose.
Keep retrieval and user-triggered agents allowed unless there is a specific reason not to.
suggested_action.mechanism: Absence does not shut the discovered gate, but it forfeits the one place to declare a sitemap and to record an intentional crawler policy, so a future change can silently remove citation eligibility.
suggested_action.verification: Request /robots.txt and confirm a 200 with text/plain and a resolvable Sitemap line.

findings.title: No usable sitemap was found
findings.evidence: No sitemap could be read. Locations tried: https://books.toscrape.com/sitemap.xml (status 404), https://books.toscrape.com/sitemap_index.xml (status 404), https://books.toscrape.com/sitemap-index.xml (status 404). Discovery fell back to following links, which found 412 URLs. This is a crawl-efficiency problem rather than a block: pages linked from the site are still reachable.

evidence_detail.method: sitemap locations from robots.txt, then conventional paths
evidence_detail.expected: at least one sitemap returning 200 and parsing as a urlset

suggested_action.summary: Publish a sitemap with accurate lastmod values and declare it in robots.txt.
how: Generate a sitemap from the publishing pipeline so lastmod reflects the real content change date rather than the build clock.
Segment it by template (products, articles, static pages) so a crawler can recrawl the fast-changing parts without refetching the rest.
Add a `Sitemap:` line to robots.txt pointing at the index.
suggested_action.mechanism: A sitemap does not unblock anything; it tells a crawler which URLs exist and which have changed, so pages that are weakly linked internally get discovered and changed pages get recrawled sooner.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the sitemap URL and confirm it returns 200, parses, and lists the canonical URL of every template.

No headless browser was available in this run to confirm directly by comparison, so this is inferred from structure rather than measured against a render.

evidence_detail.expected: no combination of these signals on a content page
evidence_detail.note: confirm with a real render comparison when a browser is available; this fallback trades recall for the ability to screen without one

suggested_action.summary: Confirm with a real browser render comparison, then server-render or pre-render the core content if confirmed.

findings.title: The copyright year lags the site's own newest content by more than a year
findings.evidence: 1 pages show a copyright year of 2003, while the newest date signal observed anywhere in the sample is 2023 -- a gap of 20 years. Example: https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: a copyright year (matched via the © symbol or the word 'copyright') compared against the newest date signal (structured data, sitemap, or Last-Modified header) found anywhere in the sample, or the audit's own crawl date if no other signal exists
evidence_detail.expected: the copyright year within a year of the site's own newest content

suggested_action.summary: Update the copyright year, ideally driven automatically from the current date rather than a hand-maintained value.
how: Generate the footer copyright year from the server's own clock at render time, so it never needs manual updating.
suggested_action.mechanism: A lagging copyright year is a weak but real signal a system may use when judging how actively a site is maintained, independent of whether the content itself is still accurate.
suggested_action.verification: Re-check the footer and confirm the year matches or exceeds the site's own newest content date.

findings.title: Sampled pages have no inbound link from any other sampled page
findings.evidence: 1 sampled pages are not linked to by any other page in this sample -- orphan-like within the sampled graph. This does not establish that the page is globally unreachable, only that no other page this audit observed points to it. Examples: https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: every internal link URL across every sampled page, normalised and compared against each sampled page's own URL
evidence_detail.expected: at least one other sampled page links to this page
evidence_detail.note: scoped explicitly to the sampled graph; a page reached only through pages outside the sample, or through a sitemap alone, would appear orphan-like here without genuinely being orphaned

suggested_action.summary: Link to these pages from at least one other relevant page in the site's own content or navigation.
how: Identify a relevant category, hub or related-content page for each listed URL.
Add a direct link to it from there.
suggested_action.mechanism: A page with no inbound link from anything else this audit sampled is reachable only through a sitemap or direct URL knowledge, which is a weaker discovery and continuation path than an in-content link from a related page.
suggested_action.verification: Re-check the site's sampled link graph and confirm at least one other page now links to this URL.

findings.title: Heading levels skip, breaking the outline
findings.evidence: 17 pages with 4 or more headings have at least one level jump of more than one step, for example h2 directly to h4. Example: https://books.toscrape.com/.

evidence_detail.method: sequence of heading levels extracted from the raw HTML, checked for jumps greater than one level, on pages with at least 4 headings
evidence_detail.expected: heading levels increase by at most one step at a time

suggested_action.summary: Fill in the skipped heading levels so the outline descends one step at a time.
how: Replace a jump such as h2 to h4 with h2 to h3 to h4, or demote the deeper heading if no intermediate section exists.
suggested_action.mechanism: A skipped level breaks the outline a machine would otherwise use to navigate straight to the section that answers a question.
suggested_action.verification: List the heading levels on the page and confirm no step exceeds one.

severity_notes: detector capped this check at low

findings.title: Pages below the homepage carry no breadcrumb markup
findings.evidence: 20 of 20 sampled non-homepage pages have no BreadcrumbList markup. Examples: https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/art_25/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: presence of a BreadcrumbList node, after full @graph traversal, on pages other than the homepage
evidence_detail.expected: BreadcrumbList markup below the homepage, where the site has a real hierarchy

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList markup reflecting each page's position in the site hierarchy.
how: Generate it from the same navigation hierarchy the template already renders as a visible breadcrumb, if one exists.
Each ListItem needs position, name and item (the URL).
suggested_action.mechanism: Breadcrumb markup gives a machine an explicit statement of where a page sits in the site's structure, which is otherwise only inferable from the URL path.
suggested_action.verification: Re-check the page and confirm BreadcrumbList markup parses and matches the page's actual position.

severity_notes: detector capped this check at low

opportunities.summary: Decide which value is current and correct.
opportunities.description: Findings from freshness-corroboration-audit and structured-data-entity-audit co-occur on overlapping pages: FRC.COPYRIGHT_YEAR_LAG, SDE.BREADCRUMB_MISSING, SDE.NO_STRUCTURED_DATA.
opportunities.rationale: Both detectors independently flagged overlapping pages (https://books.toscrape.com/, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html), which is stronger evidence of a compound, template-level problem than either finding alone.
opportunities.scope: Observed across 10 overlapping sampled page(s): https://books.toscrape.com/, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html (and more)
opportunities.mechanism: A fact contradicted across the site's own pages, alongside structured data that does not agree with itself either, means there is no single version of this fact a machine could trust even if it wanted to.
opportunities.expected_effect: Every surface stating this fact, structured or visible, states the same current value.
recommended_actions: Decide which value is current and correct.
Update every surface named in the underlying findings to match it, and reference a single source (a stable @id, or one field) going forward rather than maintaining separate copies.

opportunities.title: Treat access and render problems on the same template as one compound gate
opportunities.summary: Confirm both issues affect the same template cluster, not merely the same site.
opportunities.description: Findings from crawl-access-audit and render-readability-audit co-occur on overlapping pages: ACC.CANONICAL_MISSING, RND.HEADING_LEVEL_JUMPS.
opportunities.rationale: Both detectors independently flagged overlapping pages (https://books.toscrape.com/, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html), which is stronger evidence of a compound, template-level problem than either finding alone.
opportunities.scope: Observed across 10 overlapping sampled page(s): https://books.toscrape.com/, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html, https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/category/books/add-a-comment_18/index.html (and more)
opportunities.mechanism: A page an agent cannot reach and a page it can reach but cannot read are two different symptoms of the same outcome: the content never reaches an answer. Fixing access without fixing render, or the reverse, still leaves the gate shut.
opportunities.expected_effect: Once both are addressed on the same template, the pages in that cluster stop failing at either the accessible or the readable gate.
recommended_actions: Confirm both issues affect the same template cluster, not merely the same site.
Sequence the access fix first, since a render fix cannot be verified by an agent that cannot reach the page at all.
Re-run the audit against representative URLs from the cluster after both changes ship.
opportunities.verification: Re-run the audit against the URLs named in scope and confirm none of ACC.CANONICAL_MISSING, RND.HEADING_LEVEL_JUMPS fire again.

tracks.what: Whether the fixes from this audit held

tracks.what: Whether representative high-value pages continue to expose an observable next step

measurement_plan.caveat: Assistants personalise: two people asking the same question can get different brands and framing. A single prompt on a single day is not a measurement. Run clean sessions, repeat each prompt, and report rates with the sample size attached. The report carries a stable check_id on every finding precisely so consecutive audits can be diffed; the sequential id shifts as findings are added or resolved, check_id does not.
